title: Continuum coalescer param sweep field notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a working log of the "continuum" coalescer parameter sweep we ran to explore tradeoffs between batch growth aggressiveness, per-slot timeouts, and fairness when requests have correlated arrival jitter. The goal is to identify robust knobs that maintain p99/p99.9 SLAs under bursty, correlated traffic while keeping per-token cost reasonable.

Testbed overview:
- Date range: 2025-03-18 -> 2025-04-02 (iterative runs).
- Hardware: 1x A100-80GB per runtime shard, 4 shards used for parallel experiments.
- Model: open-llama-like 7B variant, FP16 path with INT4 quantized experiment subset. Inference engine: runtime-v2.3.1.
- Workloads: three synthetic arrival patterns: Poisson (baseline), Pareto-bursty (alpha=1.4), and correlated-cluster (clusters of requests with intra-cluster inter-arrival ~ 0-8ms, cluster inter-arrival ~ 200-1200ms).
- Payloads: short-chat (avg tokens=40), long-dialog (avg tokens=300).
- QPS targets: 50, 200, 800 to exercise light->moderate->heavy regimes.
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9 latency (ms), tail CPU/GPU utilization, batch size distribution percentiles, average tokens-per-batch, fairshare index (Jain's index computed across tenants/slots), starvation events (reqs delayed > timeout*3), throughput (tokens/s), cost proxy (tokens per GPU-second). Traces collected for sample runs with HTTP request ids to correlate queue and kernel timings.

Key knobs swept:
1) growth_alpha: how quickly the coalescer allows batches to grow within a slot window (0.2, 0.5, 1.0).
2) base_timeout_ms: per-slot maximum waiting time before flush (2, 6, 15, 30 ms).
3) deadline_scaler: multiplies request-level soft deadlines to allow preferential flush when nearing SLA (0.5, 1.0, 2.0).
4) demotion_threshold: urgency score below which requests are demoted to lower-priority lanes (0.1, 0.25, 0.5).
5) slot_affinity_window_ms: how long a request will prefer an existing slot vs joining any slot (0, 8, 32).

Representative run summary (Pareto-bursty at 200 QPS, short-chat):
- Baseline conservative settings: growth_alpha=0.2, base_timeout_ms=6, deadline_scaler=1.0, demotion_threshold=0.25, slot_affinity=8ms. Observed: p50=14ms, p95=72ms, p99=210ms, p99.9=430ms. Average batch size=3.7 tokens/batch, tokens-per-batch ~ 146. Starvation events: 4.
- Aggressive growth (growth_alpha=1.0, base_timeout_ms=6): p50 improved (11ms), p95 similar (70ms), p99 increased to 260ms, p99.9 to 540ms. Average batch size rose to 6.9. Observed starvation correlation with long-dialog co-running.
- Short timeout (base_timeout_ms=2, growth_alpha=1.0): p50 9ms, p95 48ms, p99 120ms, but throughput drops ~8% due to more kernel underutilization and smaller batches; cost proxy increases.
- Increased deadline_scaler (2.0) helped reduce p99 for latency-sensitive requests by ~18% at cost of fairness: Jain's index fell from 0.93 -> 0.81 (we saw tenants with long-dialogs being pushed later).

Unexpected observations / anomalies:
- Inter-arrival correlation amplified starvation non-linearly. When cluster sizes hit >8 requests, demotion_threshold interventions didn't prevent long-dialog requests from being perpetually deferred by a series of small high-urgency requests arriving in tight succession. We saw multi-hop starvation where a request that had been demoted continued to be bypassed across successive slots.
- slot_affinity_window_ms > 0 reduced latency variance for repeat-tenant flows (e.g., webchat sessions) because co-locating tokens in same slot kept KV cache locality and reduced kernel warmup costs. But high affinity increased contention for cold tenants and reduced perceived fairness.
- The INT4 quantized path exacerbated tail spikes under aggressive growth because kernel scheduling latency jitter became visible; smaller batches caused more frequent kernel launches and amplified variance.
- Deadline_scaler helped mostly when soft-deadlines were accurate. In runs with noisy deadline hints, the scaler created perverse scheduling where many requests near-deadline flooded the flush path at the same time causing transient tail spikes.

Microtrace case study (one p99.9 incident):
- Workload: correlated-cluster 800 QPS, mixed payloads.
- Configuration: growth_alpha=0.5, base_timeout=15ms, demotion_threshold=0.1.
- Trace: cluster of ~60 small requests arrived in 300ms. Coalescer built several large batches (size 10-14) and queued multiple long-dialog requests to later slots. A pathological sequencing of cluster arrival plus a kernel preemption (GPU context switch due to resource reclaim) produced a 9s stall for a subset of long-dialog requests.
- Root cause hypothesis: simultaneous large-batch kernel launches + KV-miss prefill for demoted long-dialogs caused memory pressure and driver-level serialization.
- Mitigation applied mid-run: reduced max_batch_slots for high-occupancy windows and raised base_timeout to flatten coalescing window; tail reduced but cost increased.

Guiding heuristics distilled so far:
- Keep base_timeout_ms small (2-8ms) for short-chat-dominant workloads to avoid kernel starvation, accept higher token cost if throughput is low.
- For mixed workloads, prefer moderate growth_alpha (0.4-0.6) and small positive slot_affinity (4-12ms) to preserve KV locality while limiting cross-tenant starvation.
- Use deadline_scaler conservatively and only when deadline signals have high precision; otherwise, treat deadline hints as noisy and fall back to urgency-percentile-based promotion.
- Introduce a sliding starvation counter per request-id that forces promotion after N bypasses (N=2-3 depending on workload) — this proved effective in toy runs to prevent multi-hop starvation.
- Prefer demotion_threshold around 0.25 for systems that serve a mix of short and long responses; lower thresholds hurt long-dialogs, higher thresholds handcuff short-chat latency.

Proposed next experiments (actionable):
1) Bounded-kernel-concurrency probe: limit concurrent kernel launches per shard to 2 and observe tail under aggressive growth_alpha across workloads. Target: verify whether driver-level serialization is root cause for p99.9 stalls.
2) Starvation counter ablation: run with the sliding starvation counter enabled vs disabled across Pareto-bursty high-QPS to quantify reduction in multi-hop starvation and cost overhead.
3) Affinity throttling: dynamic slot_affinity that scales down when Jain's fairness drops below 0.85. Measure p99 vs fairness under mixed-tenant simulation.
4) Deadline-signal quality evaluation: instrument producer (frontend) to tag a subset of requests with high-confidence deadlines; measure effectiveness of deadline_scaler only on that subset.
5) Kernel warmup amortization: attempt tiny synthetic prefill (single-token no-op) for INT4 path to keep kernel resident and measure whether p99.9 reduces without excessive overhead.

Open questions / risks to investigate:
- How to balance affinity benefits (KV locality) vs fairness in multi-tenant production—can we provide per-tenant affinity budgets?
- Is there a cheap, low-latency signal from GPU driver/runtime to detect imminent kernel preemption so coalescer can throttle growth?
- Should we capture and surface a per-request "bypass count" in tracing and egress telemetry for easier debugging?
- Cost accounting: need a clearer mapping from tokens-per-batch to real cost at scale (combine with Redwood billing model) to recommend enterprise defaults.

Operational notes (for next rollout):
- Expose knobs: growth_alpha (0.2->1.0), base_timeout_ms (2->30), demotion_threshold. Keep deadline_scaler hidden behind feature flag until we have deadline-quality telemetry.
- Add an automated canary that simulates correlated clusters every hour to detect regressions to p99.9.
- Logging: add per-slot histograms emitted every 30s with batch-size-pctiles and bypass-count distribution.

Appendix: raw numbers snapshot (selected)
- Pareto-bursty, 200 QPS, short-chat:
  - conservative: p99=210ms p99.9=430ms avg_batch=3.7 tokens/batch=146 cost_proxy=0.87
  - aggressive: p99=260ms p99.9=540ms avg_batch=6.9 tokens/batch=272 cost_proxy=0.65
  - short-timeout: p99=120ms p99.9=220ms avg_batch=2.1 tokens/batch=82 cost_proxy=1.02 (throughput -8%)

Summary (one-liner):
Aggressive coalescing reduces median latency and increases GPU utilization, but without careful starvation controls, affinity and deadline mishandling cause outsized p99.9 regressions under correlated bursts. The immediate wins are (1) starvation counter to prevent multi-hop deferals, (2) slot affinity tuned per-tenant, and (3) bounding kernel concurrency for INT4 workloads.

Notes to self:
- Push the bounded-kernel-concurrency probe today (SR-5321) and capture driver traces.
- Add bypass-count to tracing schema (small field) and include in nightly cost/latency digest.
- Follow up with SRE on a reproducible 9s stall case and GPU driver logs.

End of notes.
